title: Debug one step at a time
summary: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime.
introduction: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain debug one step at a time
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A debugger can pause a supported program and let you inspect values. A breakpoint marks a place to pause. Setup depends on the language runtime.

blocks.code:
Breakpoint before: total = price * count
Inspect: price is 3, count is 2
Step over: total becomes 6
blocks.title: Debug one step at a time

blocks.text: The debugger makes the program's state visible one step at a time. It does not decide what the correct result should be.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Predict total before stepping over the calculation.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not confuse stepping through code with proving every input is correct.
For more detail later, use this [VS Code further reading](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/getting-started).
